page.layout: One column of verse, full width; below a rule, a centred line of acrostic labels; then a stanza with a large initial; catchword at lower right.

p.i: Reliquias gentis : quam nulla extinguere posthac Hostica vis poterit.
Ista Dei bonitas semper rediviva nitescit Quum fugat astra dies.
Fida manet semper, toto constantius illa Cernitur orbe nihil.
Chara Deus mihi sors, & fundus pascere firmus, Mens modo lata canat.
In te pernitiem, si sæua pericla minentur, Spes erit usque Deus.
Hunc quicunque patrem nō ficto corde requirunt: Et prece sollicitant
Auxilium cœleste pia : facili Deus illos Adiuvat usque manu.
Spes quem p[?]scit opis divina tuta, quietum Pectus habere decet.
Promissam intrepidis decet expectare salutem Mentibus Abramidas.
Quos olim à teneris immiti colla iuvabit Supposuisse iugo,
Et ferulis assuesce Dei, queis crimina chara Tollere gentis amat.

main_text.head: IOD. CAPH. LAMED.
main_text.p: QVEM Deus sic erudiit, Triste quem pressit iugum, Esse desinit superbus,

page.notes: The initial Q of the last stanza is a large woodcut-style initial, joined to "VEM". The acrostic labels IOD. CAPH. LAMED. stand centred below a rule. Doubtful readings: "mihi sors" (long s, marked [?] in the printed form); "quem p[?]scit", where a letter is unclear between p and scit; "ficto" and "Pectus" read from a worn impression. The catchword "Et" stands alone at the lower right.
